where: k_r10.py V04: DM-ACU-ROUTE-23R notWhen acu_insulin_sick_review_signs; DM-ACU-ROUTE-24B notWhen acu_t1_acetone_bohb_normal; DM-ACU-ROUTE-23 notWhen acu_insulin_sick_bohb; k_grid floor; D-DM-41
finding: Urgency falls to nothing as the picture worsens. 23R stands down on 'a sign (an interrupting rule applies)', but the interrupting rule for acetone or dehydration on insulin (24B) is itself stood down by normal blood ketones, and 23 by bohb below 0.6. Evaluator (referral): man 30, type 1 on insulin, vomiting, capillary 5.0, bohb 0.3 -> 23R same_day; the same man also dehydrated -> fired {} (23R suppressed, 24B suppressed, 23 suppressed, 11 insufficient); with acetone instead of dehydration -> {}; at capillary 9.0 -> {} for both; acutely unwell + dehydrated, capillary 5 or 9, bohb 0.3 -> {}. Only at glucose 14 does ROUTE-11 interrupt. R10's grid script re-run on this build (r11/grid11.py, 76,800 cells): 16 monotonicity drops, all this pattern (T1 or T2 on insulin, adult and older adult, vomit -> vomit_acetone / vomit_dehyd, glucose 5, bohb 0.3: same_day -> 0). The build's own floor (k_grid) reports 0 silent, so it does not cover these cells.
why: A vomiting, dehydrated person on insulin with a normal glucose cannot keep carbohydrate down (hypoglycaemia) and normal ketones at one moment do not end the ketoacidosis risk; the pack's own source (REF-DM-ACU-SICKDAY-INSULIN) says recheck every 1 to 2 hours and seek advice early. D-DM-41, which the CSO signs, promises 'same day for ... a vomiting or acutely unwell child or insulin-treated adult with diabetes'; this patient gets nothing, and a sicker-looking patient gets less than a well-looking one.
reviewerFix: Delete acetone_breath and dehydration from 23R's notWhen (keep ketones 1.6+, urine 2+, deep breathing and drowsiness, which do interrupt), or make the notWhen read 'the interrupting rule fired' rather than 'a sign is present'. Add floor rows to k_grid for vomit_acetone and vomit_dehyd with bohb 0.3 on insulin/type 1 (min same_day), and a vignette for the dehydrated patient above.

where: k_r10.py V13: targets tgt_hba1c_tight (notWhen tgt_tight_su_ins removed; when gains only 'not insulin'); tgt_hba1c_general notWhen tgt_general_tight
finding: V13 removed the guard 'On insulin or a sulfonylurea' (tgt_tight_su_ins, added in k_r7) and put back only 'not on insulin'. A sulfonylurea user with a tight tier now gets the tight target and the general target stands down for him. Evaluator: man 40, type 2 on gliclazide, tier tight, HbA1c 6.8 -> targets [tgt_fpg_surrogate, tgt_ppg_surrogate, tgt_bp, tgt_hba1c_tight], band hba1c_control_tight 'above_target'. Same on the TS runtime (npx tsx runDiabetesPack). The tight target's own display says 'never on insulin or a sulfonylurea here'.
why: A below-6.5% goal on a sulfonylurea invites intensification exactly where the pack's source (ADA: a lower goal only where treatment carries little risk of lows) and UG-16's signed wording ('not on insulin or a sulfonylurea') say not to; 'above target' at 6.8 on gliclazide is the prompt. The display and the logic contradict each other.
reviewerFix: Restore the sulfonylurea arm: tight 'when' all + glucose_lowering_therapy not in {insulin, glibenclamide, gliclazide, glimepiride} (or restore tgt_tight_su_ins), and make tgt_general_tight read the same set so the general target shows instead. Vignette: tight + gliclazide -> tgt_hba1c_general.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-16: target tgt_hba1c_elderly_2026 (no notWhen, no tier test; supersedes tgt_hba1c_general, tgt_hba1c_older_healthy)
finding: The 2026 older-adult target ignores the agreed tier. Evaluator: man 80, frail, on gliclazide, tier avoid_symptoms, district -> targets [tgt_bp, tgt_hba1c_elderly_2026] (HbA1c below 8.0% under a plan that has no HbA1c target by design); man 66, metformin, established CVD, tier tight, HbA1c 7.8 -> tgt_hba1c_tight (below 6.5%) AND tgt_hba1c_elderly_2026 (below 8.0%) together, band hba1c_control_tight 'above_target'; same man, tier general -> the agreed general target is superseded and only the 8.0% target shows. Every other HbA1c target stands down for 'avoid symptoms' (tgt_*_avoid) and yields to an agreed tier (V14).
why: Two HbA1c goals 1.5 points apart on one screen, or an HbA1c goal under an 'avoid symptoms' plan, is the T06/U06/V02 contradiction again; the clinician cannot tell which goal the plan holds, and the agreed goal (the thing the clinician and patient decided) is silently replaced.
reviewerFix: Give tgt_hba1c_elderly_2026 the notWhen 'glycaemic_target_tier in [general, relaxed, tight, avoid_symptoms]' (as tgt_hba1c_ckd and tgt_hba1c_older_healthy have) and the confirmed-diabetes atLeast; vignettes for avoid_symptoms, tight and general at 66 with CVD.

where: k_ug2026.py D-DM-40: management DM-ACT-RX-14, DM-ACT-RX-14B (read fasting_pg only); interpretation fpg_control_who, fcap_control_who (at_target from 3.9)
finding: The older-adult floor contradicts the band beside it and never reads the meter. Evaluator (referral): man 70, gliclazide, fasting_pg 4.1 (DMV-182) -> DM-ACT-RX-14 'below ADA's goal for older adults, not at target' AND band fpg_control_who 'at_target' (TS runtime: same). District: the same man with a fasting capillary 4.1 -> RX-14 silent, band fcap_control_who 'at_target', nothing else. D-DM-40's own recommended text: 'until then the bands carry no at target below the general range for people on insulin or a sulfonylurea aged 65 or over'.
why: D-DM-40 exists because a fasting 4.2 read 'at target' in an older person on insulin; it still does, at every district site (where the meter is the only control measure), and at referral sites the screen says both 'at target' and 'not at target'. Over-treatment of older people on sulfonylureas or insulin is the hypoglycaemia harm the item was signed to prevent.
reviewerFix: Let RX-14/14B read capillary_glucose with capillary_glucose_context == fasting as well as fasting_pg, and add a band (or a band 'when') so fpg_control_who and fcap_control_who show 'below the older-adult goal' rather than 'at_target' under 4.4 (5.0 frail) for 65+ on insulin or a sulfonylurea. Vignette at district.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-05/UG-45: management DM-ACT-EDU-10B, DM-ACT-EDU-10C (kind educate: no pregnancy appliesTo, no notWhen); DM-SUS-PREG-01
finding: Prediabetes weight-loss advice is given in pregnancy, beside a gestational diabetes diagnosis. Evaluator: woman 28, pregnant 28 weeks, fasting_pg 5.8 -> who_2013_gdm met, DM-CON-PREG-01 same_day AND DM-ACT-EDU-10B 'In the prediabetes range (2026): lose 7% of body weight, 150 minutes of activity a week, and a test every year' (and DM-SUS-PREG-01 still offering an OGTT); pregnant 14 weeks, HbA1c 5.9 -> DM-ACT-EDU-10C, the same text. Woman 28, fasting 5.8, pregnancy unanswered -> EDU-10B fires (unknown read as not pregnant). TS runtime agrees.
why: A fasting 5.8 in pregnancy is gestational diabetes, not prediabetes; weight-loss advice in pregnancy is contrary to antenatal care, and the label contradicts the same-day GDM item on the same screen. HbA1c reads low in pregnancy (UG-08), so a 5.9 is not 'prediabetes' either.
reviewerFix: Give EDU-10B and EDU-10C appliesTo pregnancy 'not_pregnant' (withheld when unanswered) or notWhen pregnant; give DM-SUS-PREG-01 a notWhen 'gestational diabetes met / DM_ANY'. Vignette DMV-147 extended: assert EDU-10B silent.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-33: rules DM-ACU-ROUTE-02 and DM-ACU-ROUTE-14 (no ageBands) display; P0-01 / D-DM-32
finding: Under 16 the interrupt carries a treatment instruction. Evaluator (district): boy 8, type 1 on insulin, urine ketones 2+, capillary 25 -> interrupt DM-ACU-ROUTE-02, action '... Route now. If this site will transfer the patient, start intravenous fluids before transfer (2026: health centre III starts fluids, then refers)'; boy 8 not known diabetic, capillary 32 -> ROUTE-14 interrupt with the same sentence; boy 14, type 1, meter HI -> the same. Same on the TS runtime.
why: The pack's contract under 16 is recognition and referral only (D-DM-32, P0-01). Fluid resuscitation in childhood DKA is weight-based with a different regimen (guideline Figure 11, p. 65) and fluid errors are linked to cerebral oedema; the HC III sentence (p. 44) sits in the adult chapter. The ug2026 comparison itself asked the CSO to confirm the acute pathway carries the regimen before this ships.
reviewerFix: Append the fluids sentence only where band is adult/older_adult (an under-16 display variant without it: 'route now; the paediatric DKA pathway gives the fluids'), or split ROUTE-02/14 displays by age. Vignette: child DKA at district asserts no 'intravenous fluids' in interruptActions.

where: k_sources.py D-DM-42: rule DM-ACU-ROUTE-35 (no pregnancyUnknownCounts / unknownDisplays); semantics.pregnancyUnknown
finding: Pregnancy unanswered is treated as not pregnant for a symptomatic same-day rule. Evaluator (referral): woman 30, type 2 on metformin, vomiting, capillary 9.0, pregnant not recorded -> fired {EDU-01, EDU-02, metformin_during_acute_illness} only; the same woman with pregnant true -> DM-ACU-ROUTE-35 same_day; acutely unwell instead of vomiting -> the same split. TS runtime agrees.
why: Ketoacidosis in pregnancy comes with a near-normal glucose (the rule's own JBDS quote), so the glucose of 9 reassures no one; the unanswered pregnancy question is exactly the case where nobody has asked. The pack's semantics say only 'same-day pregnancy rules WITHOUT symptoms wait for the answer'; this one has symptoms.
reviewerFix: Set pregnancyUnknownCounts on ROUTE-35 with an unknownDisplays entry ('ask about pregnancy now; if pregnant, ketones now and same-day assessment'), at same_day. Add a women-grid row (unknown pregnancy, diabetes, vomiting, glucose 9).

where: gate-a-signoff.json D-DM-30 (signed) vs FEATURES prior_gdm (no x.restrictedClass); rules DM-SUS-PREG-UCG, DM-SUS-RISK-05; management DM-ACT-RX-15
finding: D-DM-30 was signed at GATE A: "'Could become pregnant' and previous gestational diabetes: restricted". k_signed did not apply it: prior_gdm carries no restrictedClass, so every item reading it shows its full text. Evaluator: woman 33, not pregnant, prior_intermediate_hyperglycaemia, prior_gdm -> DM-ACT-RX-15 fires ('Prediabetes with BMI 35 or more or gestational diabetes before ...'), restricted classes = {} (RX-15's hand-written neutralDisplay is never used); woman 33 pregnant 10 weeks with prior_gdm -> DM-SUS-PREG-UCG (label lists 'gestational diabetes before'), restricted {}; woman 33 with prior_gdm, 40 months since a glucose -> DM-SUS-RISK-05 'Gestational diabetes in the past ...', restricted {}.
why: A signed privacy decision is not in the content: a past pregnancy history is displayed to every role that sees the pack's output, which is what the restricted class exists to prevent.
reviewerFix: Set FEATURES['prior_gdm']['x']['restrictedClass'] = 'sexual_reproductive_health' in k_signed (citing D-DM-30) and let the build's neutral checks force neutralDisplay on RISK-05, PREG-UCG, RX-15 and any other reader. Vignette asserting 'sexual_reproductive_health' in restricted for each.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-34: target tgt_glucose_inpatient vs targets tgt_fpg_surrogate/tgt_ppg_surrogate and bands fcap_control_who/fpg_control_who
finding: Inpatients get the outpatient fasting target and its band beside the inpatient target. Evaluator: man 60, type 2 on metformin, inpatient, fasting capillary 8.0 -> targets [..., tgt_fpg_surrogate (below 7.0), tgt_glucose_inpatient (5.6 to 10.0; 'treat only if persistently above 10.0')], band fcap_control_who 'above_target'; man 60 on insulin, inpatient, fasting capillary 5.0 -> band 'at_target' although 5.0 is below the inpatient lower edge 5.6; known-diabetes inpatient with fasting_pg 8.0 -> fpg_control_who 'above_target'.
why: The quoted source (UG26-INPT-TGT) says start glucose-lowering only if persistently above 10 and treat to 5.6-10.0; an 'above target' band at 8.0 invites tightening insulin in hospital, where the guideline names hypoglycaemia as the harm (sliding scales, p. 57). Two glucose goals on one screen contradict each other.
reviewerFix: Give tgt_fpg_surrogate and tgt_ppg_surrogate notWhen care_setting == inpatient (the inpatient target applies), so their bands stop reading; optionally an inpatient band table against 5.6/10.0. Note the critically-ill 7.8-10.0 range is not modelled (no field).

where: k_ug2026.py UG-04 vs k_r5.SEMANTICS metNowSets (who_hearts_d_2020 included); newly_met / established_or_met items
finding: A point-of-care HbA1c still diagnoses through the WHO set and opens every 'met at this visit' item. Evaluator: man 45, polyuria, HbA1c 7.0, hba1c_point_of_care true -> ug_integrated_dm_2026 insufficient but who_hearts_d_2020 met, so DM-ACT-SCREEN-TB-02 and DM-ACT-INITIAL-01 ('First diabetes visit ...') fire (and any established_or_met referral would). Signoff implementedNarrower UG-04: 'Point-of-care HbA1c cannot diagnose'. Quote checked, p. 19: 'Do not use point-of-care HbA1c machines to diagnose diabetes because they provide inaccurate results.'
why: The signed rule is enforced only inside the 2026 set; because metNowSets ORs in WHO, the result the guideline says is inaccurate starts the diabetes pathway anyway.
reviewerFix: Apply the point-of-care block to the WHO set's HbA1c criteria as well (add hba1c_point_of_care absent, or a blocking caveat on hba1c when point_of_care is true), so neither metNowSet is met on a POC value. Vignette: DMV-172 with polyuria asserts SCREEN-TB-02 and INITIAL-01 silent.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-03: rule DM-SUS-INCID-02 display (notWhen only repeat_abnormal_result / pregnant)
finding: INCID-02 now says 'One result in the diabetes range: confirm it today with a second, different test ... do not leave it' and no longer carries the 'with symptoms' clause V07 kept; it fires beside a met diagnosis. Evaluator: man 45, polyuria, fasting_pg 7.4 -> who_hearts_d_2020 met AND ug_integrated_dm_2026 met, newly_met DM-ACT-INITIAL-01 'First diabetes visit' fires, and DM-SUS-INCID-02 fires telling the clinician to confirm; man 40, weakness, fasting 7.0 -> 2026 set met, INCID-02 fires.
why: Quote checked, p. 18: with classic symptoms 'a single blood glucose test (RBG >= 11.1 ... or FBG >= 7.0 ...) is sufficient to diagnose diabetes'. The screen says diagnosed and not diagnosed at once; a second visit for confirmation delays treatment and loses people to follow-up, the consequence UG-03 was signed to remove.
reviewerFix: Add to INCID-02 notWhen 'a metNowSet is met at this visit' (or the symptom list SYM() of the 2026 set), so it speaks only when one asymptomatic result stands alone. Vignette: polyuria + fasting 7.4 asserts INCID-02 silent.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-06: rules DM-SUS-PREG-01 (gestation >= 24) and DM-SUS-PREG-03 (gestation < 24)
finding: A pregnant woman whose gestation is not recorded gets no screening prompt. Evaluator (referral): woman 30, pregnant true, nothing else -> fired {}; with BMI 37 -> DM-SUS-PREG-UCG only. Both universal-screening rules read gestation_weeks and stay insufficient.
why: The signed UG-06 is 'Screen all pregnant women ... at first ANC contact'; gestation is often unknown at that contact (no dating scan), so the woman the rule is for is the one it misses. An unrecorded value silencing a prompt (review rule 2).
reviewerFix: Let DM-SUS-PREG-03 fire when gestation_weeks is not recorded (any: gestation < 24 OR gestation not recorded), with the same notWhen; or a PREG-03 variant for 'gestation unknown'. Vignette: pregnant, no gestation, no glucose -> PREG-03.

where: k_r10.py V13: targets tgt_hba1c_general (tgt_general_su_low2), tgt_hba1c_relaxed (tier_not_relaxed)
finding: R10's own V13 patient still gets no HbA1c target. Evaluator: man 50, glibenclamide, tier general, hypo_worst_12m needed_help, HbA1c 7.3 -> targets [tgt_bp] only. The general target stands down (relax reason), and the relaxed target stands down because a 'general' tier is agreed. V13's 'when.any' append to tgt_hba1c_relaxed duplicates a predicate already there and changes nothing; tgt_general_su_low2's label says 'and no tier agreed' but the criterion does not test the tier.
why: An agreed tier stood down by a relax reason leaves no glycaemic goal; DISPOSITION marks V13 FIXED.
reviewerFix: Let tgt_hba1c_relaxed fire when a general or tight tier is agreed AND a relax reason is recorded (narrow tier_not_relaxed to avoid_symptoms, or add 'and no relax reason'). Vignette with R10's patient.

where: k_r10.py V01/V04: rules DM-ACU-ROUTE-13, -23, -23D displays; DM-ACU-ROUTE-23R; abdominal pain
finding: (a) Only the labels were changed: ROUTE-13 still displays 'Diabetes with vomiting, abdominal pain or dehydration', 23 'with vomiting or abdominal pain', 23D 'vomiting or abdominal pain', and they now fire on 'acutely unwell' alone. (b) Adult type 1, acutely unwell, no glucose -> 13, 23 and 23R all same_day (three items for one event; 23 and 23R both whenever ketones are unrecorded). where: k_ug2026.py UG-11: management DM-ACT-PREG-ASA-01
finding: Fires at any gestation from 12 weeks. Evaluator: woman 30, type 2 on insulin, pregnant 34 weeks -> DM-ACT-PREG-ASA-01 'review starting aspirin to reduce the risk of pre-eclampsia'. Quote checked (UG26-PREG-ASA, p. 76): start 'from 12-16 weeks of gestation'.
why: A start prompt at 30-34 weeks is outside the source's window. Harm is limited (review with the antenatal team), but the item claims a source it does not follow.
reviewerFix: Add gestation_weeks <= 16 (a new ref) to the 'when', or reword to 'if not already started at 12-16 weeks, discuss with the antenatal team'.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-42: management DM-ACT-SCREEN-B12-02
finding: Needs months_since_b12 recorded: a person on metformin whose B12 was never measured never gets the prompt. Evaluator: man 60, type 2 on metformin, referral -> silent. DMV-194 is titled 'B12 never checked' but sets months_since_b12 60. The step also fires on any metformin, though the quote (UG26-B12) is 'if on long-term and high-dose metformin'.
why: The population the step is for (never tested) is exactly the one it misses (review rule 2).
reviewerFix: Fire when months_since_b12 >= 12 OR not recorded (or a 'never measured' option); optionally require years on metformin. Fix DMV-194's values.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-17: management DM-ACT-TEST-HBA1C-03 (fixed 7.0, REF-DM-CTRL-HBA1C-TARGET) and DM-ACT-TEST-HBA1C-01
finding: Reads 7.0% whatever target is proposed, and duplicates HBA1C-01. Evaluator: man 72, frail, metformin, HbA1c 7.6, 4 months -> target tgt_hba1c_relaxed with band 'at_target' AND HBA1C-03 'HbA1c is due (... the last, which was above 7.0%) ... every 3 months until controlled'; man 52, HbA1c 8.4, 7 months -> HBA1C-01 and HBA1C-03 both.
why: The signed recommendation was 'due at 3 months when the last HbA1c was above the proposed target'; here it contradicts the band shown and adds a duplicate prompt.
reviewerFix: Make HBA1C-03 stand down when any shown HbA1c band is 'at_target'/'in_range' (or when a relax reason/tier applies), and let HBA1C-01 yield to it.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-31/UG-32: k_clerk.DX_REFS REF-DX-GLU-HHS (33.3), REF-DX-BICARB-DKA (18), DDX-GLUCOSE-VERY-HIGH 'why'; complication_amendments dka/hhs 'what'
finding: REF-DM-ACU-HHS-GLU is now 30.0 and REF-DM-ACU-DKA-HCO3 15, but the clerking refs that declare 'mirrors' them were copied at import and still hold 33.3 and 18 (checked in memory after build: REF-DX-GLU-HHS value 33.3, REF-DX-BICARB-DKA value 18); DDX-GLUCOSE-VERY-HIGH says 'Glucose 33.3 mmol/L or more'; the HHS amendment text still says 'Glucose 33.3 or more' and the DKA amendment 'bicarbonate below 18' while citing the changed refs. The build checks only that a mirrored ref exists, not its value.
why: Two HHS thresholds in one app: at 31 the pack interrupts for HHS while the clerking differential does not list it.
reviewerFix: Rebuild DX_REFS after k_ug2026 (or read the value at emit time), add a build check that a mirror's value equals its target's, and regenerate the two amendment texts.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-22: management DM-ACT-RX-04, DM-ACT-RX-04B
finding: (a) RX-04B fires on any glucocorticoid but displays 'On high-dose steroids'. Evaluator: man 55, metformin, on_glucocorticoid -> RX-04B. (b) RX-04 now says 'the 2026 guideline starts insulin' and fires on a single meter value above 16.7 in an established patient during an acute illness: man 55, metformin, acutely unwell, capillary 17.0 -> RX-04 routine, with caveat capillary_glucose_acute_illness in force. Quote checked (p. 34): the glucose indication is 'Symptomatic patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and FBG >14, RBG >16.7, and/or HbA1c >=10%'.
why: Overstates the source for established patients and stress readings; the display claims a dose qualifier the logic does not check.
reviewerFix: RX-04B: reword to 'On a steroid: if high-dose, the 2026 guideline lists insulin' (no field for dose). RX-04: reword to 'the 2026 guideline starts insulin at diagnosis at these values; in an established patient review treatment', or skip the glucose arms when capillary_glucose_acute_illness is in force.

where: k_ug2026.py UG-01/UG-04: diagnosis_pending ug_integrated_dm_2026 (plasma and laboratory values only)
finding: The default set has no meter criterion, so at a district site it is 'unavailable' for a plainly diabetic patient. Evaluator (district): man 45, polyuria, capillary 15.0 -> who_hearts_d_2020 met, ug_integrated_dm_2026 'unavailable'. The UG-04 recommendation that was signed: 'Keep D-DM-04 (meter diagnosis) at sites without an analyser'.
why: The set labelled Uganda's default never reaches 'met' where most patients are seen; the referrals still run (WHO is in metNowSets), so the harm is a confusing display rather than a missed referral.
reviewerFix: Add the WHO set's meter criteria (with symptoms; or with a repeat) to the 2026 set at sites without lab.glucose, or label the 2026 set 'laboratory sites' in the semantics.

where: k_signed.py / k_ug2026.py: duplicates for one event
finding: Evaluator: pregnant 16 weeks, BMI 37, nothing tested -> DM-SUS-PREG-UCG and DM-SUS-PREG-03 both routine 'test for it'; man 55 metformin, albuminuria x2, no statin -> DM-ACT-RX-06 and DM-ACT-RX-06C; man 80 frail, gliclazide, no tier -> tgt_hba1c_relaxed and tgt_hba1c_elderly_2026 (both below 8.0%); man 63, eGFR 45 -> tgt_hba1c_ckd and tgt_hba1c_elderly_2026; known type 2 inpatient with a fasting_pg recorded -> DM-SUS-INPT-02 'Admitted: check a random glucose' (notWhen reads only random_pg and capillary_glucose).

where: k_ug2026.py D-DM-40: DM-ACT-RX-14 (therapy_review appliesTo not_pregnant)
finding: The older-adult floor waits on a pregnancy answer for a 70-year-old woman. Evaluator: woman 70, gliclazide, fasting_pg 4.1, pregnancy unanswered -> withheld ['DM-ACT-RX-14', ...].
why: The safety prompt the item exists for does not show until someone records 'not pregnant' for a 70-year-old.
